subject.title: [security] Semaphore redirects can replay job payloads and disclose API tokens

question: Should Semaphore enforce Crabbox’s configured-origin redirect boundary even when a caller supplies an HTTP client whose redirect callback would otherwise permit a cross-origin hop?
rationale: The README establishes the security boundary, but maintainers need to confirm the compatibility contract for caller-supplied clients and the exact policy-composition behavior before a security fix lands.

options.title: Enforce configured-origin redirects
options.body: Clone the effective client and require scheme, canonical host, and effective port to match the configured origin before also honoring any caller callback.

options.title: Honor caller redirect policy as an override
options.body: Allow a supplied callback to authorize broader redirects, accepting that callers can opt out of the documented default boundary.

recommendation.title: Enforce configured-origin redirects
recommendation.body: Clone the effective client and require scheme, canonical host, and effective port to match the configured origin before also honoring any caller callback.

likelyOwner.reason: They supplied the detailed redirect and Go-client behavior analysis; repository ownership history was not available from the provided review context.
